summary: Conjecture 7.6 of the source (the outer-connected domination number of the line graph is at most that of the middle graph) is false: for every h >= 2 the graph formed by two copies of K_{2h} joined by a three-edge path has outer-connected domination number 2h+2 for its middle graph and C(2h,2)+h+1 for its line graph (6 against 9 at h = 2), under both conventions for an empty complement. Lean proves explicit bounds giving the strict inequality for every h and infinitely many counterexample orders; the exact values are proved in the paper. Significance is low; this is a second result from section 7 of the same source as accepted 355217.
paste_summary: Refuted. For every h >= 2, take two copies of the complete graph K_{2h} joined by a path with three edges. The outer-connected domination number of its middle graph is 2h+2, while that of its line graph is C(2h,2)+h+1 (6 against 9 at h = 2), so the conjectured inequality that the line graph value is at most the middle graph value fails for infinitely many connected graphs, under either convention for an empty complement.
caveat: Low significance, and a second credit from the same source section as 355217 (user may overrule). Lean proves bounds sufficient for the refutation; exact values are in the written proof only.
title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
source: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15439)
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$, and let $L(G)$ and $M(G)$ denote its line graph and middle graph, respectively. The **line-middle graph inequality conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(L(G)) \le \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The inequality is supported by the preceding results, including strict inequality for wheels of order at least five; equality occurs for at least one connected graph of order four. A classification of graphs for which equality holds is posed separately as an open problem, while the general inequality remains open.
